title: w13 GEMM with SwiGLU epilogue
description: The fused gate/up projection [8192,4096]x[4096,28672] can compute silu(gate)*up in its epilogue (pairing gate and up columns in the same tile), writing the product next to the gate/up output kept for backward.
bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds gate/up to bf16 first and evaluates silu and the product with aten's rounding points.
dataflow: mm(w13) -> view [8192,2,14336] -> unbind -> silu, mul -> w2 GEMM.
blockers: Tile must cover matching gate and up columns (they are 14336 columns apart in the fused weight); custom epilogue GEMM.

title: Residual adds as wo / w2 GEMM epilogues
description: Both residual adds of each block (x + wo(...), h + w2(...)) can be done in the epilogue of the GEMM producing the branch output, avoiding the separate read of the branch output and the residual.
bitwise_notes: Epilogue must round the accumulator to bf16 first and then add the bf16 residual in fp32 to match <program>'s two roundings.
dataflow: wo and w2 outputs are consumed only by the residual adds.
blockers: Custom epilogue; alternative to R-12/R-13 (fuse the add into the following norm instead).

title: SwiGLU backward: two muls, silu_backward and the gate/up gradient cat in one pass
description: Backward of SwiGLU computes d_up = dh * silu(gate), d_silu = dh * up, d_gate = silu_backward(d_silu, gate) and stacks d_gate and d_up into [8192,28672]; one kernel reads dh and gate_up and writes the stacked gradient directly.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise with bf16 roundings at the same points as <program> (d_up = dh*silu(gate), d_silu = dh*up, silu_backward in fp32).
dataflow: The two mul outputs and silu_backward output feed only the UnbindBackward0 cat, whose output feeds only w13's backward GEMMs. Recomputing silu(gate) from gate_up removes the forward's saved silu output (forward-backward pairing).
blockers: Autograd materializes each gradient separately and stacks them with cat; needs a custom autograd Function (as the local_compile region would provide).

title: Rotary table gather and conjugate computed once per step instead of per layer
description: Every layer's attention gathers the same [8192,64] complex rotary rows for the same positions in forward, and every layer's backward materializes the same conjugated table twice (for dq and dk); computing the gathered table and its conjugate once per step removes 95 of 96 kernels.
bitwise_notes: Gather and conjugation are exact.
dataflow: index(freqs_cis, positions) per layer (identical inputs) ; _conj -> clone per q/k per layer (identical).
blockers: Each layer's rope module traces its own gather; a program pass must recognize identical inputs (same placeholder table and positions).

title: RMSNorm backward + residual-gradient accumulation
description: Each norm backward writes dx [8192,4096] and then add_ accumulates it into the residual gradient; the norm backward can add the incoming residual gradient in its epilogue and write the sum once.
bitwise_notes: Row reductions (dot(dy*w, x)) and the weight-gradient column reduction must follow the quack kernel's order.
dataflow: The norm's dx is consumed only by the add_ into the residual-gradient buffer.
blockers: Autograd accumulates the two gradient contributions of the residual stream with a separate add_; needs a fused norm-backward-with-residual Function.

title: lm_head weight gradient: one GEMM over all chunks writing the reduce-scatter buffer
description: The eight chunk weight-gradient GEMMs ([128256,1024]x[1024,4096], first mm then 7 addmm) each read and write the full fp32 [128256,4096] accumulator (4.2 GB per chunk), which is then copied unchanged into the reduce-scatter buffer; one K=8192 GEMM (or a persistent accumulator that is the reduce-scatter buffer) avoids both.
bitwise_notes: Changes the fp32 accumulation order from 8 sequential K=1024 GEMMs (addmm into fp32) to one K=8192 GEMM; bitwise only if the GEMM keeps the same per-chunk accumulation order.
dataflow: All eight GEMMs write the same accumulator, consumed only by the reduce-scatter copy-in, whose dim-0 chunking of a contiguous [128256,4096] tensor is a no-op layout change.
blockers: Batching needs all eight chunks' bf16 dlogits (2.1 GB) alive at once, against the purpose of the chunked loss; aliasing the accumulator to FSDP's reduce-scatter buffer needs FSDP API support.

title: Attention-backward postprocess fused with RoPE backward and d_qkv concat
description: The attention backward converts its fp32 dq/dk/dv accumulators to bf16 in three postprocess kernels, after which RoPE backward re-casts dq/dk to fp32, rotates, casts back and concatenates into d_qkv; the postprocess can apply the inverse rotation and write d_qkv [8192,8,6,128] directly.
bitwise_notes: Bitwise only if the epilogue reproduces the bf16 rounding of dq/dk before the fp32 rotation.
dataflow: flash_bwd -> postprocess (dq,dk,dv -> bf16) -> _to_copy f32 -> mul(conj freqs) -> _to_copy bf16 -> cat -> wqkv backward GEMMs.
blockers: Attention library internals (flash_attn cute postprocess kernels); needs a custom epilogue <callback>.

title: FSDP all-gather copy-in: fp32->bf16 cast fused with copy into all-gather buffer
description: Before every all-gather the fp32 sharded parameters are cast to bf16 into temporaries and then copied into the flat all-gather input buffer; a single foreach kernel can cast straight into the buffer.
shapes_dtypes: layer shard fp32 27.26M elems -> bf16 all-gather input; tok_embeddings / (norm, lm_head) shards 65.7M elems
bitwise_notes: Elementwise round-to-nearest bf16 cast and a copy; bitwise identical.
dataflow: The bf16 temporaries written by the first _foreach_copy_ are read only by the all_gather_copy_in _foreach_copy_.
blockers: FSDP mixed-precision cast (FSDPParam.all_gather_inputs) and copy-in are separate library steps.

title: RoPE forward: q/k/v contiguous copies + fp32 complex rotation of q and k
description: Each attention splits the wqkv output [8192,6144] bf16 into q/k/v, makes each contiguous, gathers the rotary table for the positions, and rotates q [8192,32,128] and k [8192,8,128] via cast-to-fp32, complex multiply and cast-back (10 kernels); one kernel can read the qkv rows once and write rotated q, k and contiguous v.
bitwise_notes: Casts and complex multiply only; the fused kernel must evaluate the complex product with the same operation order/FMA contraction as aten's complex mul in fp32.
dataflow: mm(wqkv) -> view/split -> clone(q), clone(k), clone(v) -> _to_copy f32 -> view_as_complex -> mul(freqs[index(positions)]) -> view_as_real -> _to_copy bf16 -> _varlen_attn. The three clones and two rotations are siblings over the same qkv rows.
blockers: The rotary table gather is done per layer from the same positions; a fused kernel should take positions + table directly. Attention needs contiguous q/k/v in this layout (varlen packed).

title: Chunked cross-entropy: logits cast, log_softmax, NLL and their backward per 1024-token chunk
description: For each of the 8 chunks of 1024 tokens, the bf16 logits [1024,128256] are cast to fp32, log-softmaxed, NLL-reduced, and immediately differentiated (nll_loss_backward zero-fill + scatter, log_softmax backward, cast back to bf16) in 6 large and 4 scalar kernels; a single kernel can read the bf16 logits once and emit the loss contribution and the bf16 logit gradient.
bitwise_notes: Row max / sum-exp reductions must use the same reduction order as cunn_SoftMaxForward; the gradient (exp(logp)*sum(g) - g) then follows pointwise; the per-chunk loss scalar adds must keep chunk order.
dataflow: mm(lm_head) bf16 -> _to_copy f32 -> _log_softmax (saved) -> nll_loss_forward -> div(token count) -> add (loss accumulator); ones_like -> div -> nll_loss_backward (memset 525MB + scatter) -> _log_softmax_backward_data -> _to_copy bf16 -> lm_head backward GEMMs. The backward for chunk i runs right after its forward, so the fp32 log-probs never need to leave the kernel.
blockers: The chunk's backward is driven by autograd inside the loss forward; fusing forward and backward needs the upstream gradient scale (1/token count) available at forward time, which it is in this <program>.

title: SwiGLU backward: two muls + silu_backward + stack
description: In each feed_forward backward, the gradient of silu(gate)*up ([8192,14336] bf16) is computed by two separate multiplies, a silu_backward and a stack that interleaves d_gate/d_up into [8192,2,14336]; one elementwise kernel can read dY, gate, up and the saved silu once and write the stacked gradient directly.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise only; must keep aten's rounding points (silu value rounded to bf16 before dY*silu; dY*up rounded to bf16 before silu_backward).
dataflow: mul(dY, silu_saved) -> d_up; mul(dY, up) -> silu_backward(., gate) -> d_gate; stack([d_gate, d_up], -2) -> w13 backward GEMMs. All intermediates single-use.
blockers: None structural; the strided gate/up halves (unbind of the fused w13 output) are what make the separate aten kernels fall back to the slow non-vectorized path.

title: w13 GEMM with SwiGLU epilogue
description: The w13 projection [8192,4096]x[4096,28672] can apply silu(gate)*up in its epilogue, writing gate_up (saved for backward) and h without a separate pass.
bitwise_notes: Epilogue must round the GEMM accumulator to bf16 before silu (as <program> does) and keep the same GEMM K-order.
dataflow: w13 output feeds only the SwiGLU (and is saved for its backward).
blockers: Needs a GEMM with a paired-column epilogue (gate and up columns 14336 apart) and bitwise-identical main loop to cuBLAS/nvjet.

title: Residual add in the wo / w2 GEMM epilogues
description: The attention output projection (wo) and the FFN down projection (w2) each write [8192,4096] bf16 that is immediately added to the residual stream; the GEMM epilogue can add the residual and write h directly.
bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds the accumulator to bf16 before adding the residual (aten adds two bf16 tensors).
dataflow: mm(wo or w2) -> add(residual, .) -> h -> norm.
blockers: Competes with the add+RMSNorm fusions for the same add; the norm needs the whole row, which a GEMM tile of N=4096 rarely covers.

title: Weight unpack folded into GEMM operand loads (consume the all-gather buffer in place)
description: Instead of copying the gathered weights out of the rank-major all-gather buffer, the wqkv/wo/w13/w2/lm_head GEMMs and the norms read their operand tiles straight from the 8 per-rank chunks, removing the unpack copies entirely.
bitwise_notes: GEMM must accept a chunked operand (8 base pointers / TMA descriptors); results bitwise equal if the GEMM's K-order is unchanged.
dataflow: all_gather output -> (copy) -> weight -> mm. The copy has a single consumer per parameter.
blockers: Needs a GEMM that takes a rank-chunked B operand (grouped/TMA multi-descriptor), and for w13 the Shard(1) chunks interleave within each of the gate/up halves; the backward GEMMs also reuse the unpacked weights, so the copy must either stay or both forward and backward GEMMs read the chunked buffer (which must then stay alive).

title: Token embedding gather + layer-0 attention_norm
description: The embedding gather writes h0 [8192,4096] which layer 0's attention_norm immediately re-reads; the norm can gather rows directly (still writing h0 for the residual).
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm reduction order.
dataflow: h0 feeds attention_norm and the first residual add.
blockers: Crosses the embedding/decoder-layer and FSDP unit boundary.

title: Cross-entropy forward + backward per loss chunk
description: For each 1024-token chunk, the [1024,128256] bf16 logits are upcast to fp32, log_softmax'd, gathered by nll, then backward zeroes a fp32 gradient, scatters, runs log_softmax backward and casts back to bf16; a single fused CE kernel reads the bf16 logits once and writes bf16 dlogits plus the scalar loss.
shapes_dtypes: logits bf16 [1024,128256] (+fp32 copy, log-probs, fp32 grad), labels int64 [1024] -> dlogits bf16 [1024,128256]
bitwise_notes: logsumexp over V=128256 in fp32 must reproduce PyTorch's log_softmax reduction tree; the nll gather/scatter and the 1/num_tokens scaling are pointwise.
dataflow: The fp32 logits, log-probs and fp32 dlogits are each consumed by exactly the next op; the chunk's backward runs immediately after its forward, so forward and backward can share one kernel.
blockers: CrossEntropyLoss is compiled by the 'loss' local_compile region in the default recipe (off here); bitwise reduction order over the vocab.

title: Final norm weight-gradient fp32 cast + reduce-scatter bucket copy
description: The final norm's 4096-element bf16 weight gradient is cast to fp32 and then copied into its own reduce-scatter bucket by a second kernel (plus a host-to-device metadata copy); one kernel can write the fp32 bucket directly.
bitwise_notes: Exact cast + copy.
dataflow: _fused_rms_norm_backward (dweight) -> _to_copy f32 -> _pre_bucket_reduce_scatter -> reduce_scatter.
blockers: Launch-bound; a better fix is putting this 4096-element parameter in the same bucket as lm_head (both are packed separately today).

title: lm_head grad accumulator aliased to the reduce-scatter buffer (last chunk GEMM + copy)
description: The fp32 lm_head gradient [128256,4096] is copied by chunk_cat into an [8,65667072] buffer with the identical memory layout; letting the last chunk's addmm accumulate in (or the accumulator be) that buffer removes the 4.2 GB copy.
bitwise_notes: Removes a byte-for-byte fp32 copy; the GEMM is unchanged, so numerics are unchanged.
dataflow: chunk_cat input is the final accumulator and its output feeds only the reduce-scatter.
blockers: Requires FSDP to accept a pre-placed gradient in its reduce-scatter buffer (or to skip chunk_cat when the layout already matches).

title: lm_head input-gradient written in place into the hidden-state gradient buffer
description: Each chunk's lm_head input gradient [1024,4096] bf16 is produced by a GEMM and then copied into a zero-initialized [8192,4096] buffer; the GEMM can write its rows of the buffer directly and the zero-fill is unnecessary because the 8 chunks cover all rows.
bitwise_notes: Writing the GEMM result to a row slice is bitwise identical.
dataflow: zeros_like(h) ; mm(dlogits, W) -> copy_ into slice [i*1024:(i+1)*1024] -> final norm backward.
blockers: The copy is generated by the chunked loss's manual gradient assembly; the zero-fill is only removable if every row is provably written.

title: Token-embedding gather + layer-0 attention_norm
description: The embedding gather writes the [8192,4096] bf16 hidden state and layer 0's attention_norm re-reads it; one kernel can gather rows, write the residual and the normalized output.
bitwise_notes: Norm reduction order as quack; the gather is exact.
dataflow: embedding(table, ids) -> h0 -> _fused_rms_norm -> wqkv GEMM; h0 also the residual.
blockers: None structural; tiny.

title: Attention residual add + ffn_norm RMSNorm
description: h = x + attn_out is written to memory and immediately re-read by ffn_norm; a fused add+RMSNorm reads x and attn_out once and writes h (residual) and the normalized [8192,4096] output.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm's row sum of squares must use the same reduction order as the existing quack RMSNorm kernel.
dataflow: h feeds ffn_norm and the next residual add; attn_out (wo output) feeds only the add.
blockers: Bitwise match of the quack RMSNorm reduction; the add sits in the block's forward between two modules.

title: Attention-backward accumulator zero-fill folded into the preprocess kernel
description: Each attention backward launches five memsets (two 51MB fp32 accumulators and three small buffers) before its preprocess kernel (rowsum of dO*O); the preprocess kernel can zero the accumulators in the same pass.
shapes_dtypes: memsets 2x51380224 B + 3x278528 B; preprocess reads O,dO bf16 [8192,32,128], writes f32 [32,8192]
bitwise_notes: Inside the attention library; zero-fill is exact.
dataflow: memset(dq_accum), memset(dk/dv accum), memset(semaphores) ; flash_bwd_preprocess(O, dO) -> flash_bwd.
blockers: Attention library internals (flash_attn cute); requires a library change.

title: FSDP all-gather unpack: split_with_sizes_copy + w13 re-layout cat
description: After each block's weight all-gather, the rank-major bf16 buffer [8,27264000] is copied out into six per-parameter tensors, and the w13 weight is then copied a second time from rank-major [16,1792,4096] into [2,14336,4096]; a single copy can write every parameter, including w13, directly in its final layout.
bitwise_notes: Pure data movement; exact element placement (rank-major chunks, Shard(1) for w13) must be reproduced.
dataflow: all_gather_into_tensor_out -> wait -> view [8,-1] -> split_with_sizes_copy(out=6 buffers) -> (w13) split(2) -> cat(dim1) -> reshape [28672,4096] -> mm. Each output is consumed only by its parameter's GEMM/norm.
blockers: Unpack is generated by the bucketing pass and the w13 re-layout by DTensor Shard(1) redistribution; fusing needs the w13 placement known to the unpack.

title: FSDP all-gather copy-out: split_with_sizes_copy + w13 Shard(1) re-assembly
description: After each layer's all-gather (forward and backward prefetch), the [8, 27.26M] bf16 buffer is split into per-parameter tensors and w13 is then re-assembled by a second cat from its eight [2,1792,4096] shards; the copy-out can write w13 in its final [2,14336,4096] layout directly.
bitwise_notes: Order-sensitive copy only (no arithmetic); bitwise trivially once indices match.
dataflow: split_with_sizes_copy writes w13's per-rank pieces into a temporary [8,2*7340032] view that only the following cat reads.
blockers: FSDP copy-out path (split_with_sizes_copy + Shard(dim!=0) fix-up) is library-owned; needs a copy-out that handles non-zero shard dims in one pass.

title: w2 dgrad GEMM with SwiGLU-backward epilogue
description: The w2 input-gradient GEMM produces dh [8192,14336]; its epilogue can load gate_up and write the stacked [8192,28672] SwiGLU gradient directly.
bitwise_notes: GEMM output must be rounded to bf16 (dh) before the pointwise backward math.
dataflow: dh is consumed only by the SwiGLU backward.
blockers: Custom GEMM epilogue with two extra operand loads; bitwise main loop.

title: RoPE backward + dQKV assembly in one pass
description: Backward of RoPE upcasts dq and dk to fp32, multiplies by the conjugated cache, casts back to bf16, and SplitWithSizesBackward concatenates dq, dk, dv into [8192,8,6,128]; one kernel can read dq/dk/dv and write the fused dqkv.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise conj-multiply in fp32 plus casts; same arithmetic-order caveat as R-08.
dataflow: Each cast/mul output is consumed only by the next op; the final cat feeds only wqkv's backward GEMMs.
blockers: Autograd materializes each step; needs a custom autograd Function for the rope+split.

title: w2 input-gradient GEMM with SwiGLU-backward epilogue
description: The w2 input-gradient GEMM [8192,4096]x[4096,14336] produces dY for SwiGLU; its epilogue can read gate, up and silu for the same tile and write the stacked [8192,2,14336] gradient directly.
bitwise_notes: Bitwise if dY is rounded to bf16 in the epilogue before the SwiGLU backward math.
dataflow: mm(dout, W2) -> dY -> mul/mul/silu_backward/stack -> w13 backward GEMMs; dY is also needed by the w2 wgrad GEMM (mm(mul_out^T... ) uses dout, not dY), so dY has no other consumer.
blockers: Custom epilogue GEMM reading three extra operands per tile.

title: FSDP reduce-scatter copy-in: w13 grad re-layout + bf16->fp32 chunk_cat
description: Per layer, the bf16 weight gradients (wqkv, wo, w13 [2,14336,4096], w2, two norms) are first re-laid out (w13 chunked along dim 1 and concatenated to [16,1792,4096]) and then copied with an fp32 upcast into the [8, 27.26M] reduce-scatter input; one pass can write the fp32 buffer straight from the gradients.
bitwise_notes: Pure data movement with an exact bf16->fp32 widening; bitwise identical as long as every element lands in the same rank-major slot.
dataflow: cat output [16,1792,4096] bf16 is consumed only by _chunk_cat, whose output is consumed only by the reduce-scatter; both are index permutations plus a cast of the same 218M gradient elements.
blockers: Owned by FSDP (foreach_reduce / chunk_cat); the Shard(1) w13 path is a separate cat before the chunk_cat. Needs a custom copy-in kernel or a chunk_cat that accepts a per-parameter shard dim.

title: Attention residual add + ffn_norm
description: In each decoder block, h = x + attn_out ([8192,4096] bf16) is written and immediately re-read by ffn_norm; one kernel can add, write h (still needed as residual and for backward), and write the normalized output and rstd.
bitwise_notes: RMSNorm row reduction order must match quack's kernel; the add is bf16 pointwise ahead of it.
dataflow: mm(wo) -> add(x, .) -> h -> _fused_rms_norm(h) -> w13 GEMM; h also feeds the next residual add.
blockers: Norm is a library CuTe DSL kernel; fused add+norm variant needed.

title: Layer weight-gradient GEMMs writing fp32 directly into the reduce-scatter buffer
description: The four weight-gradient GEMMs per layer write bf16 gradients that FSDP immediately re-reads to build the fp32 reduce-scatter input; their epilogues can write (bf16-rounded, widened) fp32 values at each rank's offset of the reduce-scatter buffer.
bitwise_notes: Epilogue must round each gradient to bf16 before widening to fp32 to match <program> (wgrad in bf16, then chunk_cat upcast).
dataflow: Each weight gradient is consumed only by the reduce-scatter copy-in (AccumulateGrad is a no-op hand-off).
blockers: Requires FSDP to expose its reduce-scatter buffer before backward and GEMMs with a row-blocked scattered output layout (each rank's slice is a separate address range).

title: FSDP reduce-scatter pack: weight-grad fp32 casts, w13 re-layout and bucket copy
description: After each decoder block's backward, its six bf16 weight gradients (wqkv 6144x4096, wo 4096x4096, w13 2x14336x4096, w2 4096x14336, two 4096 norm weights) are cast to fp32 one by one, the w13 gradient is re-laid out rank-major with a second full copy, and everything is copied again into the flat fp32 reduce-scatter buffer; one kernel can read each bf16 gradient once and write fp32 straight into its rank-major slot of the buffer.
bitwise_notes: Pure cast (bf16->fp32 is exact) plus copies; the only constraint is reproducing the exact rank-major placement of each element in the bucket, which is deterministic index math.
dataflow: mm(wgrad, bf16) -> _to_copy(f32) [-> view [2,14336,4096] -> split(1792,dim1) -> cat(dim0) for w13] -> _pre_bucket_reduce_scatter (chunk_cat into f32[8*27264000]) -> reduce_scatter. Every intermediate has exactly one consumer, so the chain collapses to a single gather-cast-scatter.
blockers: The cast, the w13 re-layout and the bucket copy come from three layers of software (FSDP grad redistribute, the DTensor Shard(1) placement of w13, and the bucketing pass); a fused kernel needs the bucket layout (per-rank offsets) at program-pass time. The w13 Shard(1) placement is what forces the extra re-layout copy.

title: Fused linear cross-entropy (lm_head forward + CE + lm_head dgrad) per chunk
description: Per chunk, lm_head [1024,4096]x[4096,128256] produces logits that only feed the CE, and the CE gradient feeds only lm_head's input-gradient GEMM; a fused linear-CE never writes the 263 MB bf16 logits or the fp32 intermediates.
bitwise_notes: Needs both GEMMs and the vocab reduction inside; logits are never materialized, so bitwise needs the same per-tile reduction order as the unfused path (hard).
dataflow: logits -> CE -> dlogits -> dgrad GEMM; nothing else reads logits/dlogits (dlogits also feeds the weight-gradient GEMM, R-19).
blockers: dlogits is also needed by the lm_head weight-gradient GEMM; a fused kernel must either recompute logits for it or emit dlogits. Bitwise is very hard.

title: SwiGLU computed in the w2 GEMM A-operand prologue
description: Instead of writing h = silu(gate)*up [8192,14336] and reading it back, the w2 projection can compute h tile by tile while loading its A operand from gate_up.
bitwise_notes: Prologue must produce the same bf16 h values (silu in fp32, bf16 round, multiply, bf16 round) before feeding the MMA.
dataflow: h is consumed by the w2 GEMM and saved for w2's weight gradient; recomputing h from the saved gate_up in backward removes the saved copy (forward-backward pairing).
blockers: h is also needed by w2's weight-gradient GEMM in backward: either still write h (costs 235 MB, stays flop-bound) or recompute it in the backward prologue. Needs a GEMM with a fused elementwise A-prologue.

title: Final norm backward fused with the chunked-loss gradient accumulation
description: The chunked loss zero-fills an [8192,4096] gradient buffer and copies each chunk's hidden-state gradient into it, then the final RMSNorm backward reads it; the norm backward can consume the chunk gradients directly (row-wise), so the buffer fill and copies disappear.
bitwise_notes: Norm weight-gradient reduction over 8192 rows must keep the quack kernel's order; row-wise dx is order-free.
dataflow: The accumulation buffer is written by 8 copies and read once by the final norm's backward.
blockers: The chunk loop and the decoder backward are separate autograd graphs joined by _DecoderOutputGradientBackProp; the norm's weight gradient needs a cross-chunk reduction.

title: Flash-attention backward prologue/epilogue kernels folded into neighbours
description: Around each attention backward, accumulators are zeroed by memsets, a preprocess kernel computes rowsum(dO*O) (and zeroes dQ accumulation), and three postprocess kernels convert fp32 dQ/dK/dV accumulators to bf16; these can be folded into the wo dgrad epilogue (rowsum) and the RoPE-backward pass (conversion).
shapes_dtypes: O, dO bf16 [8192,32,128]; dQ accum fp32 [8192,32,128]; dK/dV accum fp32
bitwise_notes: Inside the attention library; the dQ fp32 accumulation order is set by the main kernel and must be preserved.
dataflow: dO (wo dgrad output) and O feed the preprocess; the postprocess outputs feed only RoPE backward / the dqkv cat.
blockers: Library-owned (flash_attn.cute via torch varlen_attn); changing the kernel boundary needs the library to expose fp32 accumulators or accept a fused epilogue.

title: RMSNorm backward + residual-gradient accumulation add
description: At every attention_norm and ffn_norm backward ([8192,4096] bf16), the normalized-input gradient is written out and then added to the residual-stream gradient by a separate kernel; one kernel can compute the norm backward and add the incoming residual gradient before writing.
shapes_dtypes: dy, x, residual-grad bf16 [8192,4096]; rstd f32 [8192,1]; weight bf16 [4096] -> dx bf16 [8192,4096], dweight bf16 [4096]
bitwise_notes: Row reductions (dy*w*x dot) and the column reduction for dweight must keep quack's reduction order; the residual add is a bf16 pointwise epilogue on the rounded dx.
dataflow: mm(dgrad of w13 or wqkv) -> _fused_rms_norm_backward -> dx -> add(residual grad, dx) -> next GEMMs. The add's other input is the running residual-stream gradient; dx has no other consumer.
blockers: The add is created by autograd's gradient accumulation (multiple uses of the residual tensor), outside any module; the norm backward is a CuTe DSL kernel (quack) so the add must become its epilogue.

title: wqkv GEMM with split + RoPE epilogue
description: The fused qkv projection can write q, k (rotated) and v in their separate contiguous layouts from its epilogue.
bitwise_notes: Epilogue rounds to bf16 before the fp32 rotation, matching <program>.
dataflow: wqkv output feeds only the split/rope chain.
blockers: Custom epilogue with a position-indexed cache load and head-dependent output routing.

title: SwiGLU forward+backward pair: recompute silu in backward instead of saving it
description: With fused SwiGLU forward and backward kernels, the forward no longer needs to write silu(gate) [8192,14336] bf16 and the backward no longer reads it, since the backward kernel already reads gate; this pairs the forward and backward of each feed_forward.
bitwise_notes: Recomputing silu in fp32 then rounding to bf16 reproduces the saved value exactly.
dataflow: forward silu output is saved only for backward mul(dY, silu); the backward kernel reads gate anyway.
blockers: memory_policy 'none' saves every forward activation; changing what is saved is a joint forward/backward decision.

title: Embedding backward writing fp32 straight into the reduce-scatter buffer
description: The embedding backward zero-fills a 1.05 GB bf16 [128256,4096] gradient, scatter-adds the 8192 token gradients (sort + segment sum), and FSDP then copies it with an fp32 upcast into the reduce-scatter buffer; one pass can zero-fill and scatter directly into the fp32 buffer.
bitwise_notes: Deterministic sorted segment sums in bf16 (same token grouping and order), then an exact widening to fp32.
dataflow: The bf16 embedding gradient is consumed only by the reduce-scatter copy-in.
blockers: embedding_dense_backward (deterministic) and FSDP's chunk_cat are separate library steps; bitwise requires the bf16 segment-sum rounding before widening.

title: wqkv GEMM epilogue emitting rotated q/k and contiguous v
description: The wqkv projection [8192,4096]x[4096,6144] can apply RoPE in its epilogue and store q, k, v in the contiguous per-head layouts attention consumes, removing the 10 prologue kernels.
bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds the accumulator to bf16 before the fp32 rotation, matching the unfused rounding points.
dataflow: mm(wqkv) -> split/clone -> rope -> attention.
blockers: The backward needs the rotated q/k (saved for attention backward) - unchanged; needs a GEMM with a custom epilogue and positional table input.

title: SwiGLU forward: silu(gate) * up in one pass
description: In each feed_forward, silu reads the strided gate half of w13's [8192,2,14336] output and writes a [8192,14336] bf16 tensor that mul immediately reads with the up half; one kernel reads gate_up once and writes the product.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise; reproduce silu in fp32 then bf16 rounding of silu(gate) before the multiply.
dataflow: silu output is consumed by mul (and saved for MulBackward0); gate and up come from the same w13 output.
blockers: <program> runs two ATen kernels on a non-contiguous gate view (non-vectorized path, ~1.7 TB/s). The recipe's default local_compile region 'fused_binary_activation' covers this but is off in this run.

title: FSDP all-gather copy-in: cast each layer's fp32 shard once per step, reuse it for the backward re-gather
description: Each layer's fp32 parameter shard is cast to bf16 and copied into the all-gather input twice per step (forward gather and backward re-gather) with identical results; casting once into a persistent per-layer bf16 all-gather input removes the backward pair of copies.
shapes_dtypes: layer shard fp32 [27264000] -> bf16 all-gather input [27264000], 2 gathers per step
bitwise_notes: The fp32 shard does not change between forward and backward of a step, so the cached bf16 values are bitwise identical.
dataflow: Forward and backward copy-in read the same unchanged fp32 shard and write the same bf16 all-gather input values.
blockers: Keeping the bf16 all-gather input (54.5 MB per layer, 1.7 GB for 32 layers) alive from forward to backward trades memory for the copies; FSDP frees it after each all-gather.

title: lm_head weight-gradient fp32 cast fused into the per-chunk wgrad GEMM epilogue
description: For each loss chunk, the lm_head weight gradient [128256,4096] is produced in bf16 by a GEMM and then cast to fp32 for the reduce-scatter by a separate 3.15GB-traffic kernel; the GEMM epilogue can round to bf16 and store fp32 directly.
bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds the fp32 accumulator to bf16 before widening to fp32.
dataflow: mm(dlogits^T, h) bf16 -> _to_copy f32 -> reduce_scatter -> add_ (accumulate across chunks).
blockers: Needs a GEMM epilogue with custom rounding; the reduce-scatter per chunk (8x the gradient traffic) is itself a structural cost of chunking the loss before reduce-scatter.

title: QKV split copies + complex RoPE forward in one pass
description: After wqkv, q is made contiguous, k and v are copied, and RoPE upcasts q and k to fp32, multiplies by the complex cache gathered at positions, and casts back; one kernel can read the fused [8192,6144] qkv once and write rotated q, rotated k and v.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise; the fp32 complex multiply must use the same operation order/FMA contraction as the <program> complex-mul kernel (the compiled real-arithmetic path is only within 1 bf16 ulp).
dataflow: Each copy/cast output is consumed only by the next op in the chain; q and k use the same gathered cache rows (horizontal), v only needs the copy.
blockers: <program> ComplexRoPE uses view_as_complex/complex mul; the 'rope' local_compile region is off here. Bitwise needs matching the complex multiply arithmetic.

title: lm_head per-chunk reduce-scattered gradient accumulation folded into the reduce-scatter
description: The fp32 lm_head gradient shard [16032,4096] reduce-scattered for each loss chunk is added into a running fp32 accumulator by a separate kernel (7 times); the reduce-scatter's own reduction can take the accumulator as one more operand.
bitwise_notes: Changes where the add happens inside the reduction; bitwise only if the accumulator is added after the cross-rank sum, in the same order.
dataflow: reduce_scatter(chunk i) -> wait -> add_(acc, .) -> ... -> final grad.
blockers: Requires a reduce-scatter with an accumulate-into-output epilogue (not available in NCCL); alternatively accumulate the 8 chunk wgrads in fp32 before a single reduce-scatter, which changes summation order (not bitwise) but removes 7 of 8 reduce-scatters.
source: torchtitan/experiments/graph_trainer/chunked_loss.py (chunk loop, lm_head grad reduce-scatter per chunk)

title: lm_head GEMM + cross-entropy + input-gradient GEMM per chunk (logits never written)
description: For each 1024-token chunk, the lm_head projection to 128256-way logits, the cross-entropy and its gradient, and the input-gradient GEMM can run as one fused linear-cross-entropy kernel that keeps the logits tile on chip, instead of writing and re-reading [1024,128256] bf16/fp32 tensors five times.
bitwise_notes: Online-softmax reductions change the reduction order versus cunn_SoftMaxForward; bitwise identity would require replicating the row-wise reduction tree across vocab tiles, which is hard.
dataflow: mm(h, W^T) -> CE chain (R: chunked CE) -> mm(dlogits, W) -> dh; the wgrad GEMM (dlogits^T h) also needs dlogits, so either it is fused too (recompute logits per tile) or dlogits is still written once.
blockers: The wgrad GEMM needs dlogits for all vocab rows; a fused kernel must either also produce dW (accumulating across chunks) or still write dlogits once. Bitwise parity with the unfused softmax is unlikely.

title: FFN residual add + next layer's attention_norm (or final norm)
description: The block output h + ffn_out of layer i is written and immediately normalized by layer i+1's attention_norm (the final model norm after layer 31); fusing the add into the next norm saves a write+read of [8192,4096].
bitwise_notes: Same reduction-order requirement as R-12.
dataflow: The block output feeds the next block's attention_norm and its residual add only.
blockers: Crosses the transformer-block (and FSDP unit) boundary; <program> module structure keeps them in different module calls.

title: FFN residual add + next layer's attention_norm (final norm after layer 31)
description: The block output out = h + ffn_out ([8192,4096] bf16) is written by one kernel and re-read by the next block's attention_norm (or the final norm); one kernel can do both across the layer boundary.
bitwise_notes: Same as the intra-layer add+norm.
dataflow: mm(w2) -> add(h, .) -> out -> next layer _fused_rms_norm(out) -> wqkv GEMM; out also feeds the next residual add.
blockers: The next layer's FSDP all-gather unpack sits between the two ops in program order (no data dependency).

title: Weight-grad GEMM epilogues writing fp32 directly into the reduce-scatter bucket
description: The four weight-gradient GEMMs of each block (wqkv, wo, w13, w2) can store their results, rounded to bf16 and widened to fp32, straight into their rank-major slots of the reduce-scatter buffer, removing the cast, re-layout and pack copies.
bitwise_notes: Bitwise if the epilogue rounds to bf16 before widening.
dataflow: mm(wgrad) -> _to_copy -> (cat) -> _pre_bucket_reduce_scatter -> reduce_scatter.
blockers: GEMM output must be split into 8 rank chunks at arbitrary row (and for w13, Shard(1) dim) boundaries; norm-weight grads come from a different kernel.

title: FSDP all-gather input packs (fp32 shard -> bf16 slice) batched into one launch per step
description: Before every block's weight all-gather, its fp32 parameter shards are cast to bf16 into this rank's slice of the gather buffer by one multi-tensor kernel per bucket (34 per step, about 1.3x roofline each); since all shards are available at step start, the 34 casts can run as one multi-tensor launch.
bitwise_notes: fp32 -> bf16 casts only (round-to-nearest-even, identical in any kernel).
dataflow: param shard (placeholder) -> _pre_bucket_all_gather (cast + copy into slice) -> all_gather_into_tensor_out (in place). The 34 packs have no data dependencies on each other or on the forward.
blockers: All 34 gather output buffers (436MB each per layer) would be allocated at step start instead of just before each layer's all-gather; with memory_policy 'none' they all stay alive until backward anyway, so peak memory changes little, but the bucketing pass emits one pack per bucket by construction.

title: SwiGLU forward: silu + mul on the strided gate/up halves of the w13 output
description: Each feed_forward applies silu to the gate half and multiplies by the up half of the fused w13 output [8192,2,14336] bf16 in two kernels that both read stride-28672 views; one kernel can read gate/up once and write silu (kept for backward) and the product.
bitwise_notes: Pointwise; product must use the bf16-rounded silu value as aten does.
dataflow: mm(w13) -> view [8192,2,14336] -> unbind -> silu(gate) ; mul(silu, up) -> w2 GEMM. silu output also saved for backward (memory_policy none).
blockers: None structural.

title: Varlen attention metadata (cu_seqlens) from positions in one kernel
description: Before the forward, the decoder builds packed cu_seqlens from positions with ~25 tiny ops (eq, cumsum, where, full, arange, scatter_, sums and async asserts); with deterministic algorithms scatter_ becomes a sort-based index_put taking ~0.65 ms for 8192 elements.
bitwise_notes: Integer cumsum/scatter; exact. scatter_ order only matters for the discarded overflow slot.
dataflow: All intermediates are consumed within the metadata builder; output is a [19] int32 cu_seqlens.
blockers: Deterministic mode routes scatter_ through index_put_ with sorting; a dedicated kernel (or a non-scatter formulation) is needed.

title: Token-embedding backward: zero-fill, deterministic scatter-add, fp32 cast and bucket copy
description: The embedding weight gradient [128256,4096] is zero-filled in bf16, scatter-added from the [8192,4096] token gradients via sort/segment kernels, cast to fp32 and then copied again into the reduce-scatter buffer; one pass can write the fp32 bucket directly (zeros for untouched rows, segment sums for touched rows).
bitwise_notes: Deterministic segment sums (sorted by token id) must keep the same per-row accumulation order and the bf16 rounding before widening.
dataflow: embedding_dense_backward (memset 1.05GB, radix sort, compute_grad_weight, sum_and_scatter) -> _to_copy f32 -> _pre_bucket_reduce_scatter (chunk_cat) -> reduce_scatter.
blockers: Deterministic-algorithms mode selects the sort-based embedding backward; the bucket pack is from the bucketing pass.

title: RoPE backward: inverse rotation of dq/dk + concat into d_qkv
description: Each attention backward rotates dq [8192,32,128] and dk [8192,8,128] by the conjugate rotary table (cast to fp32, materialize conj, complex multiply, cast back) and concatenates dq/dk/dv into the [8192,8,6,128] wqkv-output gradient (9 kernels); one kernel can read dq/dk/dv once and write d_qkv.
bitwise_notes: Casts + complex multiply with the conjugated table; same rounding points as the aten chain.
dataflow: _varlen_attn_backward -> (dq, dk, dv) -> _to_copy f32 -> mul(conj(freqs) cloned) -> _to_copy bf16 -> cat(dim=heads-group) -> wqkv backward GEMMs.
blockers: None structural.

title: RoPE cache gather, position bounds check and cache conj computed once per step
description: Every layer re-checks positions <= max position, gathers cache[positions] into [8192,1,64] complex64, and in backward re-materializes the conjugated cache twice; these depend only on positions and are identical for all 32 layers.
bitwise_notes: Pure gathers/compares/conj; bitwise identical.
dataflow: positions and the rope cache are the same tensors for every layer; the gathered cache and its conj have no layer-dependent input.
blockers: Each layer owns its RoPE module and cache buffer; hoisting needs the decoder to precompute the gathered cache (or the fused rope kernel to gather inline, which R-08/R-10 already assume).
